title: Engineering Mathematics
objectives:
This course provides mathematical techniques in the more advanced areas of mathematics that are
of most relevance to engineering disciplines.
syllabus:
- Fourier Series, Integrals, and The Fourier Transform
Introduction to Fourier Series, Convergence of Fourier Series and Their Integration and
Differentiation, Fourier Sine and Cosine Series, Other Forms of Fourier Series, Frequency and
Amplitude Spectra of a Function, Double Fourier Series. The Fourier Integral, The Fourier
Transform, Fourier Cosine and Sine Transforms, Sturm–Liouville Problems, Eigenfunctions, and
Orthogonality
- Partial Differential Equations
The Method of Characteristics, Wave Propagation and First Order PDEs, Generalizing Solutions,
Conservation Laws and Shocks, The Three Fundamental Types of Linear Second Order PDE,
Classiﬁcation and Reduction to Standard Form of a Second Order Constant Coefﬁcient Partial
Differential Equation, Boundary Conditions and Initial Conditions, Waves and the OneDimensional Wave Equation, The D’Alembert Solution of the Wave Equation and Applications,
Separation of Variables, Some General Results for the Heat and Laplace Equation, An
Introduction to Laplace and Fourier Transform Methods for PDEs
- Complex Analysis
Complex Functions and Mappings, Limits, Derivatives, and Analytic Functions, Harmonic
Functions and Laplace’s Equation, Elementary Functions, Inverse Functions and Branches,
Complex Integrals, Contours, the Cauchy–Goursat Theorem, and Contour Integrals, The Cauchy
Integral Formulas, Some Properties of Analytic Functions, Complex Power Series and Taylor
Series, Uniform Convergence, Laurent Series and the Classiﬁcation of Singularities, Residues and
the Residue Theorem, Evaluation of Real Integrals using Residues, The Inversion Integral for the
Laplace Transform, Conformal Mapping, Conformal Mapping, and Boundary Value Problems
- Calculus of Variations
Maximum or minimum of an Integral, Euler’s equations, Lagrange’s equations, Sturm–Liouville
systems, and Rayleigh-Ritz methods.
textbooks:
1. Michael Greenberg, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 2nd edition, 1998
2. Erwin Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, tenth edition, 2011
